prospect.name: Nic
prospect.location: Perth, Western Australia, Australia (working away regionally at time of call)
prospect.occupation: Carpenter ("chippy by trade"), works away from home on regional jobs
prospect.family_status: Partner (not married, a personal trainer, currently stay-at-home); one son under a year old
prospect.training_background: Ex Australian Rules football at a high level; calisthenics; some Muay Thai; trains with partner at the gym on weekends, at least twice a week; self-taught kettlebell work copied from Trevor's Facebook posts; snowboarding, surfing, fishing, swimming
prospect.medical: Historic buckled knee causing depression fractures (femur into tibia) and meniscus disruption, eight months off work; later AC joint (shoulder) damage aggravated by golf and a snowboarding trip. States he has been injury-free for about two years, with occasional knee niggles and a stiff back when inconsistent. Rep asked about injuries and prospect confirmed both are resolved.

signals: Self-directed and capable — already replicating the coach's free Facebook workouts himself and has a personal-trainer partner producing weekly plans on an app for free
Arrived anchored to a price he researched himself: "I typed into Google what it might cost to go down this endeavor and that's where I got the 200-a-month answer"
Expected an app with video clips and occasional lives, not one-to-one coaching
Not a pure bargain hunter — he grants the value ("there's no price on your health") and the blocker is genuine household cashflow, so confidence is moderate

goals.text: Get stronger and broader through the back, shoulders, glutes and lower back without conventional bodybuilding
Build a "bulletproof", injury-proof body so old knee and shoulder problems do not return
Master kettlebell technique and understand the movements properly rather than copying posts
Regain consistency and a structured routine that survives working away from home
Build mental strength and discipline that carries into work and family life
Be a father his son copies — actions over words — and a role model to people around him
Absorb enough knowledge to eventually help others in the fitness industry alongside his partner

pains.text: Since becoming a dad his time is limited and he cannot carve out training time when he is at home
Consistency "has fallen right off" since a Fiji holiday about six weeks ago; comfortable rather than progressing
No structure or game plan — copying Trevor's Facebook routines onto paper is slow and he does not know if he is doing them correctly
Working away with no gym access breaks his routine; training in a small room is unmotivating
Does not have the knowledge or foundation to make kettlebell work land properly
Residual knee niggles and a stiff back when he is not moving enough
Feels guilty about going backwards while people he previously inspired have moved ahead of him
Single household income, renting, saving toward a house purchase and funding partner's business — limited discretionary money

objections.raw_quote: Well, the initial reaction is, it's a lot of money, obviously, but there's no price on your health.
objections.rep_response: Did not defend the price; asked a future-pacing worth question ("six months, 12 months from now... would it be worth six grand to you?"), got a yes, then moved to isolate finances.

objections.raw_quote: we're not necessarily in a great financial position for that to be an easy decision
objections.rep_response: Asked what he had left over at the end of the month; prospect disclosed a $200/month budget ceiling; rep abandoned the $6,000 offer and presented the Primal Instinct University tier at $200/month or $2,000/year.

objections.raw_quote: So my money is her money, our money. We will need to have a conversation of how we can make that work.
objections.rep_response: Asked what her reaction would be and whether she would be supportive; explored whether he felt selfish; never asked whether it was genuinely a joint decision or offered a deposit-and-refund path.

objections.raw_quote: I don't really want to make a decision right here right now I just want to sleep on it and we can make it work.
objections.rep_response: Explicitly declined to push ("I'm not going to force you into doing anything"), reframed it as uncertainty, ran the skydiving/plane analogy, then accepted the delay.

objections.raw_quote: I don't really have any of my kettlebells, my gym environment, my normal ability to start a new endeavor... This is just more of a discovery call to see how I can make this work and map it out.
objections.rep_response: Agreed with the objection — "Does sound fair in the sense of you don't have anything with you at the moment" — and booked a 15-minute setup call for Sunday instead of closing.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No structured plan was built. Rep said only: "most guys, they just put it all up front. We don't have anything, like, set in stone... we would just have a conversation about it and see what would work."
offer.guarantee_mentioned: "After that, you'll stay in the community. And of course, if you had done everything that you needed to do in those six months, but we just haven't touched a goal specifically yet, he would stay with you until you have."

evidence: Verbally agreed to the low tier: "Awesome. Yeah. Awesome. Let's get started with that."
Immediately walked it back: "I still need to run this with my partner and make a game plan with her... I don't really want to make a decision right here right now I just want to sleep on it."
No payment taken and no payment link sent — only a calendar invite for a 15-minute Sunday setup call and an informational link about Primal Instinct University
Counter-evidence: the rep himself framed Sunday as "get you set up", so intent to buy the $200/mo tier is high; but nothing was collected or committed on this call
outcome.next_step: 15-minute call Sunday 17:00 Perth time with Richard (partner invited) to set up the Primal Instinct University membership; informational link sent in the meantime.

notable.note: The $6,000/6mo offer was abandoned mid-call and replaced live with a much cheaper community product (Primal Instinct University, $200/mo or $2,000/yr) as soon as the prospect named a $200/month budget. The rep never ran the money play to completion — no cards, credit or assets were explored — and later conceded the timing objection outright rather than working it. This is a substantially out-of-ICP prospect (carpenter, single household income, renting) who was downsold rather than disqualified.

quality.notes: Frequent single-turn inversions throughout — e.g. at 00:01:43 the rep's own framing question "So Simon, what can we potentially actually help you with?" is attributed to Nic, and at 00:32:17 the rep's answer is labelled Richard while the question is labelled Nic. Role was read from content. Connection also dropped repeatedly ("you cut out for a second"), and there is at least one garbled machine artefact around 00:26:27.
